text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.38% today to $151.37, continuing a strong rally that has added 10% over the past two weeks. The immediate catalyst was oil prices holding firm—US crude at $107.89 and global benchmark Brent at $115.22—despite a Saudi-Iran de-escalation meeting on October 26th. The broader driver of this two-week climb is Middle East geopolitical tension: Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, Trump's public accusations against Iran, and spillover worries about regional supply disruptions have kept oil prices elevated and benefited major US oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The deeper context is that Middle East risk is now reshaping energy markets in ways that favor US producers. News coverage notes the Iran conflict is boosting demand for US liquefied natural gas and drawing investor attention to "under-the-radar" energy plays—a category that includes large integrated oil companies with global reach. As long as regional tensions sustain higher oil prices, refiners and producers with diverse supply sources benefit.
